mechanism_narrative: The four-week TRANSIT series is recovering from -33.6 to -28.0 percent of baseline while RETAIL_REC has stopped falling, and transit footfall leads discretionary retail visits by roughly two to three weeks; continued transit normalization therefore lifts RETAIL_REC above its trailing four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -29.1 at t-1w to -28.0 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved from -35.9 to -34.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is at or below its trailing 28-day mean while TRANSIT weekly means hold at or above -28.0 percent of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS weekly means crossing above +10 percent of baseline mark a durable shift of discretionary leisure time back into public space; the same leisure demand spills into retail-and-recreation venues within two weeks, so RETAIL_REC rises.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above +10 percent of baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS climbed from 6.6 at t-2w to 10.1 at t-1w and 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: After any week with PARKS above +10 percent of baseline, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is lower than the 14 days preceding that crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery requires transit and office mobility to move together: when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES weekly means both improve versus the prior week, commuter footfall compounds into retail visits, producing higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week by at least 1 point

failure_condition: In weeks where both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by at least 1 point, the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL stays pinned between +5.4 and +6.0 percent of baseline across all four weeks, showing work-from-home habits have not decayed; with WORKPLACES still near -34 percent, weekday daytime retail demand stays suppressed and RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near -25 percent while RETAIL_REC sits near -35 percent; this roughly ten-point essential-versus-discretionary gap narrows as households shift trip budgets back toward discretionary retail, and it closes upward through RETAIL_REC gains over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -24.6 versus RETAIL_REC at -34.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Over the next 14 days the GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC gap widens further instead of narrowing.

mechanism_narrative: Under a policy regime of relaxing restrictions, the binding constraint on retail is the office-reopening threshold; once WORKPLACES weekly means rise above -30 percent of baseline, weekday retail traffic follows within four weeks and lifts RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -30 percent of baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered from -41.6 at t-2w to -33.9 at t-1w and -34.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after WORKPLACES first exceeds -30 percent of baseline is not higher than over the 28 days before that crossing.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has reached +11.9, a four-week maximum, which typically marks the peak of the outdoor-activity season; as outdoor leisure demand peaks and rolls over, discretionary spending rotates into indoor retail-and-recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC in the following weeks.
